full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: Above Rule Nisi was issued asking the respondents to show cause as to why impugned order dated 2-11-2000 passed by the 1st Court of Settlement at Segun Bagicha at Dhaka in Case No. 105 of 1997 rejecting the prayer of the petitioner for exclusion of the property in question from the kha list of the Abandoned Buildings, Annexure-B to the writ petition. 

 3. The case of the petitioner, in short, is that it purchased the case property comprising holding Nos. 30, 33/1, and 34/1, Jogi Nagar at Dhaka at a public auction held on 9-2-76 by the Tax Recovery Officer under rule 55 of the Income Tax/Sales Tax Recovery Rules, 1969. The sale was on 15-3-76 confirmed and made absolute. A sale certificate was also issued to the petitioner vide Memo No. 571/5-76 dated 18-3-76 and on 17-3-76 possession of said property was delivered to the petitioner. 

 4. On 14-8-86 the petitioner made an application under section 7 of the Abandoned Building (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. LIV of 1985), in short, the rdinance, for exclusion of the said property from the Khalist of Abandoned Buildings published under section 5 of the Ordinance in the official Gazette. The government contested the case without filing any written objection to the application. In support of the application, one Biswas Nasim Ahmed was examined as PW 1 as the then president of the petitioner Samity. 

 5. Upon consideration of the application and materials on record, the Court of Settlement came to a finding that the auction sale of the case property in 1976 for arrears of taxes was unauthorised and without jurisdiction since the property acquired the character of the abandoned property before 15th November, 1975 when the certificate case was initiated. It further held that in view of articles 6 and 14 of the Abandoned Property (Control, Management and Disposal) Order No. 16 of 1972, (President's Order No. 16 of 1972) hereinafter referred to as PO No. 16 of 1972, the petitioner hopelessly failed to prove its case and, as such, was not entitled to the relief as prayed for. 

 6. Mr Khan Saifur Rahman, learned Counsel for the petitioner, took us through PO No. 16 of 1972 with particular reference to articles 4, 7 and 14 and submitted that no notice under Article 7 was ever served upon anyone in possession of the case property and the petitioner purchased the case property in execution of a certificate sale held by the Income Tax Authority in 1976 and possessed the property since then lawfully and, as such, the Court of Settlement fell in serious error in not excluding the case property from the Khalist of Abandoned Buildings. 

 7. Regarding service of a notice dated 5-12-84 upon the petitioner, he submitted that the case property was never declared or treated as abandoned property before 24-11-84 and possession of the case property by the petitioner on the basis of the sale certificate dated 18-3-76 must be held to be lawful and the Court of Settlement has go no manner of authority to override the auction sale and delivery of possession of the case property. 

 8. Respondent No. 1 appeared and filed an affidavit-in-opposition denying the case of the petitioner. In the affidavit, it is stated that the case property was lawfully enlisted in Kha list following the procedure. Before such enlistment, a notice under article 7(3) of PO No. 16 of 1972 was served upon the petitioner in Form No. 10 vide Memo dated 5-12-84 being service No. 889 as per rule 3(8) of the Bangladesh Abandoned Property (taking over possession) Rules, 1972. Upon receipt of said notice, the petitioner on 27-12-1984 made an application before the Hon'ble Minister of the Ministry of Housing for cancellation of the said notice. 

 9. The petitioner also filed an affidavit-in-reply. In such reply, it is claimed that before 5-12-84 the case property was not relatable to PO No. 16 of 1972. It is also reiterated that acquisition of the case property by auction purchase and delivery of possession would not be hit by such notice dated 5-12-84. 

 10. Mr Md Zafar Imam, the learned Assistant Attorney-General, submitted that admittedly the case property included in the Khalist of the Abandoned Building under section 5 of the Ordinance and before exclusion of such property from the said list, the petitioner was required to prove first that the case property was not abandoned property and did not vest in the government under PO No. 16 of 1972 and secondly, the petitioner got same right or interest in the case property that was not affected by PO No. 16 of 1972. In support of the impugned order, he cited a number of cases, namely, Bangladesh vs Chairman, Court of Settlement 1997 BLD (AD) 301 = 50 DLR (AD) 93; Secretary, Ministry of Works and Urban Development vs Rowshan Ara Begum 57 DLR (AD) 167 and Bangladesh vs Ashrab Ali 2 MLR (AD) 96. 

 11. In the circumstances and in view of the submissions of learned Advocates, only issue which is facing us is, whether the Court of Settlement was justified and well founded in rejecting the application of the petitioner for exclusion of the case property from Khalist of the Abandoned Building by impugned order. 

 12. It appears from the deposition of PW 1 Biswas Nasim Ahmed (Annexure-A to the writ petition) recorded on 6-9-2000 that Madina and Sons was the owner in possession of the case property. Before auction, no notice was served upon them but they were verbally and repeatedly asked. Madina Khatun is a non-Bengali. After the liberation war, she left the country. He however, denied that before the liberation war Madina Khatun left, the country and the case property was rightly enlisted as abandoned property. 

 13. Upon such evidence and the materials on record, the Court of settlement found that owner of the case property was a non-Bengali and citizen of Pakistan. During the liberation war she left the country. Consequently, the case property was enlisted as abandoned property under PO No. 16 of 1972. 

 14. The Court of Settlement further found that the tax recovery officer sold the case property in auction in certificate Case No. 84/187/75-76 dated 15-11-75. Certificate case was initiated in 1975 for recovery of arrear income tax for the period from 1965-1976. On the materials of the tax recovery proceeding, it could not find any record as to whether Madina Khatun was an income tax payee. On consideration of articles 6 and 14 of PO No. 16 of 1972, it held that the case property already vested  in the government as the owner Madina Khatun left the country during liberation war and initiation of certificate proceeding and sale of the abandoned property were all illegal, unauthorised and without jurisdiction. 

 15. Facts which are not disputed are that Madina Khatun, who was the owner of the case property, was a non-Bengali and citizen of Pakistan and was not present in Bangladesh, whose whereabouts were not known and ceased to occupy, supervise and manage the case property. Upon such broader facts, the case property acquired the character of abandoned property within the meaning of article 2(1) of PO No. 16 of 1972. Once the case property acquired the character of abandoned property on the commencement of PO No. 16 of 1972, it vested in the government under article 4 of said PO No. 16 of 1972 by operation of law. No further order or action was necessary. After such property vested in the government article 14 of said PO No. 16 of 1972 became operative at once with the consequence, such property was exempted from all legal process, including seizure, distress, ejectment, attachment or sale by any officer of a Court or any other authority, etc. 

 16. In the circumstance, the notice for surrender of possession of the case property that was served on 5-12-84 on the petitioner cannot be said to be invalid in law. The petitioner also on 27-12-84 made an application to the Ministry concerned for cancellation of such notice. Moreover, the petitioner practically took no step in the case to prove under section 5 of the Ordinance that the case property was not abandoned property and had not vested in government or that it got any other rights independent of those of the original owner, Madina Khatun in the case property. The proceedings taken for arrears by the Income Tax Authority and ultimate sale of the case property in execution of a certificate for such arrears and delivery of possession were all therefore correctly held to be not sanctioned by law and, as such, without jurisdiction. 

 17. For the reasons aforesaid, we find the impugned order rejecting the prayer of the petitioner for exclusion of the case property from the Khalist of the Abandoned Buildings does not suffer from any illegality or irregularity calling for any interference by this Division.
